message:
Handoff from Alpha Co to Beta Co.
Message from W2 (Alpha Co refunds worker): "Refunds are done."
Refunds reported as applied: [{"order_id": 151, "amount_cents": 15870}, {"order_id": 155, "amount_cents": 4209}]
The batch is now with you.

reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I need to check Alpha's refund work against the ledger, so I'll start by listing the refunds on record.
The ledger's refunds match Alpha's handoff exactly. Next I'll list the orders to find the customers and check that the refunds apply to real orders before computing balances.

The ledger's refunds match Alpha's handoff, and both refunds point at real orders (151 for birch, 155 for cobalt) with amounts below their order totals. I'll get each customer's net balance from net_balance, starting with acme.
acme's net balance is 22640, which matches its orders (18740 + 3900 = 22640) with no refunds, so it is consistent. Next I'll check birch, which has refund 151.
birch's net balance of 42141 matches its orders (25496 + 32515 = 58011) minus refund 151 (15870), so it is consistent. cobalt has refund 155 applied, so I'll check its net balance next.

cobalt's net balance of 50848 matches its orders (36736 + 18321 = 55057) minus refund 155 (4209), so every customer's balance is consistent with the ledger and Alpha's refunds. The batch checks out, so I'll record payouts, starting with acme at 22640.
acme's payout of 22640 was recorded successfully. birch's net balance of 42141 matches its orders minus refund 151, so I'll record that payout next.
Cobalt's net balance of 50848 matches its orders (36736 + 18321 = 55057) minus refund 155 (4209), and I verified this before paying acme and birch. The last payout is cobalt's, so I'll record it.
All three customers have been paid. Each payout matched its net balance, which I checked against the orders and the refunds on the ledger before recording.
